Salama pledged twice under the tree, a feverish bedouin's pledge was not cancelled, a child was blessed instead, pledging for worldly gain was condemned, and women pledged by words only.
The Prophet thought of appointing Abu Bakr, who received public allegiance and to whom a woman was referred; Umar weighed naming a successor, and twelve rulers will be from Quraish.
The Prophet said he almost ordered the houses of men absent from congregational prayer burned, and that they would come to Isha for a meaty bone.
After Ka'b bin Malik and others stayed behind from Tabuk, the Prophet forbade Muslims to speak to them for fifty nights, then announced Allah's acceptance of their repentance.
The Prophet would join every battle but for men without mounts who hate staying behind, and would love to be martyred in Allah's cause, revived and martyred again and again.
Had the Prophet gold like Mount Uhud, he would love to give it all away within three days, if anyone accepted it, keeping only enough to pay debts.
The Prophet wished he had not brought his sacrificial animal (Hadi), so he could end ihram with the people, whom he had told to use their ihram for Umrah.
Unable to sleep, the Prophet wished a righteous companion would guard him and Sa'd came, while Bilal longed to spend a night in a Meccan valley.
One may wish to be like only two: a man given the Quran who recites it night and day, and a man given wealth who spends it rightly.
The Prophet forbade longing for or praying for death, for a good person may do more good and an evildoer may repent; Anas and Khabbab held back.
Carrying earth on the day of the Confederates, the Prophet said that without Allah they would not be guided, give charity or pray, asking tranquillity as the enemy had rebelled.
Do not long to meet the enemy, but ask Allah for safety.
Discussing a li'an case, Ibn Abbas said the Prophet's words about stoning a woman without proof concerned one whose open misbehaviour aroused suspicion.
When the Prophet delayed the Isha prayer until women and children slept, he said he would order it at that hour were it not hard on his followers.
Were it not hard on his followers, the Prophet would have ordered them to use the siwak.
The Prophet forbade continuous fasting (wisal), saying his Lord feeds him and gives him drink, and when people persisted he fasted it with them until the crescent appeared.
Aisha learned the outer wall, left out for lack of money, is the Ka'bah's, and but for her people's recent ignorance the Prophet would include it and lower the gate.
But for the emigration, the Prophet would have been one of the Ansar, and he would take the Ansar's valley if people took another.
The Prophet sent young men who missed their families home to teach them, telling them to pray as they saw him pray, call the adhan, and let the eldest lead.
Bilal's adhan at night does not stop suhur, for it lets night worshippers return to eat and sleepers wake; eat and drink until Ibn Um Maktum's adhan.
Told he had prayed five rak'at of Zuhr, and confirming Dhul-Yaddain's report that he had stopped at two, the Prophet made two prostrations of forgetfulness, completing the shortened prayer first.
When the qibla was changed to the Ka'bah, as the Prophet had wished, a man's report turned the worshippers at Quba, and some Ansar, towards it mid-prayer.
When a man announced that all alcoholic drinks were prohibited, Abu Talha had Anas break the jars of date drink he was serving.
The Prophet sent Abu Ubaida to the people of Najran as a truly trustworthy man, calling him the trustworthy one (Amin) of this nation.
Umar and an Ansari friend took turns attending the Prophet, each telling the other what he had heard from him.
When a commander ordered his soldiers into a fire, the Prophet said had they entered they would have stayed in it, for obedience is only in what is good.
For a labourer's illegal intercourse with his employer's wife, the Prophet judged by Allah's Book: ransom returned, a hundred lashes and exile for him, stoning for her on confession.
Az-Zubair answered the Prophet's call three times at the Trench and was named his helper (hawari), and Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman were given glad tidings of Paradise.
Umar found the Prophet in an upper room with a black slave at the top of the stairs, asked through him for permission, and was admitted.
The Prophet sent a letter to Khosrau through the ruler of Bahrain, Khosrau tore it up, and the Prophet reportedly invoked Allah to tear them to pieces.
The Prophet had a man of Aslam announce on Ashura that whoever had eaten should fast the rest of the day and whoever had not should complete the fast.
The Prophet told the Abd Al-Qais delegation that belief in Allah means testifying to Him and His Messenger, prayer, zakat and a fifth of booty, and forbade four drinking vessels.
When companions stopped eating meat on hearing it was mastigure, the Prophet told them to carry on, for it is lawful, though not among his own foods.
A Jew told Umar his people would have made a festival of the day the verse perfecting the religion came, and Umar said it came on Arafat day, a Friday.
Umar urged holding to the Book that guided the Prophet, who prayed for Ibn Abbas to be taught it, and Ibn Umar pledged obedience by Allah's Laws and Sunnah.
The Prophet was given concise speech of wide meaning, victory through awe and, in a dream, the world's treasure keys; unlike earlier prophets' miracles, his gift was revelation.
Umar said the Prophet and Abu Bakr must be followed, Quran and Sunna strengthen honesty, the best speech is Allah's Book, the best way Muhammad's, and heresies the worst.
All the Prophet's followers enter Paradise except those who disobey him, for obeying Muhammad is obeying Allah, as shown in parables of a banquet's inviter and a naked warner.
When some Arabs reverted to disbelief after the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr insisted, against Umar's doubt, on fighting those who separated zakat from prayer, and Umar saw he was right.
Uyaina accused Umar of giving too little and judging unjustly, but Umar held back when Al-Hurr recited the verse bidding forgiveness and turning from the foolish, keeping to Allah's Book.
